findings: The identity and original workbook and supplement hashes match the frozen JAR deposit. I independently read the original workbook, author data-description sheet (p. 3), online Appendix A1 (p. 2) and the published Chen, Jermias and Panggabean article (DOI 10.1111/1475-679X.12102, pp. 138–139).

All 60 participants and the six required variables survive the native SAS import. Category and covariate values agree exactly with the workbook. The largest fixation-ratio difference is 1.2e-16 from numeric representation. The native Stata batch completes and its executable statements match the three cells of the clean notebook.

Table 5 has two primary within-group goodness-of-fit tests. Above the mean, 23 consistent and 10 inconsistent decisions yield χ²(1) = 5.1212, p = .0236. Below the mean, 17 and 10 yield χ²(1) = 1.8148, p = .1779. These reproduce both published tests.

Table 6 reports seven effects of one repeated-measures ANCOVA with residual df = 55. Independent subject-mean and within-subject-difference regressions recover F = 6.6826 (favored measure), .0917 (presentation), 1.4928 (experience), .1514 (gender), .2122 (measure × presentation), 2.2058 (measure × experience) and 2.5238 (measure × gender). The seven native F and p values agree at the precision of the published table. H2 is supported and the H3 interaction is nonsignificant.

Both primary Table 5 tests and all seven Table 6 effects were evaluated. Their nine result records describe two contingency tests and one ANCOVA. The printed Table 6 measure-by-format mean square of .12 differs from the recomputed .01153. Its F and p values agree.

The two Appendix A1 median-split checks are supplementary. The 21/9 count reproduces χ² = 4.80, and the 19/11 count implies χ² = 2.1333, p = .1441, where the appendix prints 2.10. Both published significance decisions hold.

The reproduction starts with the author-prepared participant workbook. Raw eye-tracking videos and frame tagging, original SPSS syntax and cross-software execution are unavailable in the deposit. Manipulation checks, secondary analyses and independent raw-data preparation lie outside the reviewed baseline. The approved files contain source, documentation and aggregate tables.
